info.title: BytNode Crypto Market Data API
info.summary: Crypto market data aggregated across the major venues, derivatives, order flow, options, macro, ETF and on-chain — for developers and AI agents.
info.description:
**BytNode is a crypto market-data API built for developers and AI agents.** One key gives you market data aggregated across the major crypto venues, derivatives positioning, order flow, options, macro, ETF and on-chain fundamentals — 129 REST routes, a consolidated real-time WebSocket and a native MCP server, all behind one consistent contract.

## Why BytNode

- **Aggregated across the major venues, not one exchange.** Spot and perpetual futures markets are consolidated into one number per metric: volumes are summed, rates are open-interest weighted, prices volume weighted — and the method is documented for every metric.
- **Depth on the assets that matter.** 22 pairs: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE, BNB, TRX, SUI, HYPE, XLM, XMR, LINK, ADA, LTC, UNI, GRAM (ex-TON), AVAX, HBAR, NEAR, TAO, plus USDC and USDT spot pairs. This is a deliberate choice: together these assets are about 93 % of the total crypto market capitalisation (measured on 2026-09-30: 2.69 of 2.88 trillion USD), and each of them gets every family of data from every venue that lists it — quality and depth on the assets people actually trade, instead of thin coverage of thousands of tickers.
- **Twelve data families in one API.** Prices and candles, individual trades, order book, order flow (CVD, trade candles), funding, basis, open interest, liquidations and liquidation heatmap, tokenomics, sentiment, macro (FRED + intraday), spot ETF fundamentals (SEC EDGAR), options (OI, IV, max pain, greeks), Bitcoin network, Ethereum fundamentals, on-chain valuation, and 19 server-side technical indicators. Many providers sell these as separate products; here they share one key, one envelope and one set of conventions.
- **Honest numbers.** Every bucketed or history row says whether it is final (`is_closed`); every empty answer says why (`unavailable`: `not_applicable`, `no_api_key`, `no_data`); every numeric field has a documented unit.
- **Made for AI agents.** A native MCP server (3 tools, 60 fields), `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`, this OpenAPI contract with units and real examples, one-request snapshots of up to 48 fields, and stable machine-readable error codes.
- **Priced for builders.** A free plan (10,000 requests/month), then Traders from 6.95 USD/month, Financial from 19.95 USD/month and Startup from 99.95 USD/month (billed yearly), with history depth and families growing with the plan. See https://bytnode.com/pricing.

## Quick start

1. Create a free key at https://bytnode.com/sign-up.
2. Send it in the `X-API-KEY` header:

```
curl -H "X-API-KEY: $BYTNODE_API_KEY" "https://api.bytnode.com/v1/funding/rate?symbol=BTCUSDT"
```

## Conventions

- **Envelope.** Every success is `{status: "ok", server_time, data_type, data}`, plus the effective `symbol`, `timeframe`, `asset`, `series` or `market` when the route has them. The shape of `data` follows the path: an OBJECT (or `null`) for the latest value of a metric; a LIST (most recent first, or oldest first with `order=asc`) for every `/history` route and every series route — `/v1/klines`, `/v1/trades/{spot,futures,large}`, `/v1/trades-kline/futures/seconds`, `/v1/liquidations/events`, which are series by nature (candles, trades, events, one row per second). A `/history` envelope gives the step of its rows in `timeframe`, even when the route takes no `timeframe` parameter (`1d` for a daily series, `8h` for funding). Collections are lists too: `/v1/symbols`, `/v1/etf/fundamentals`, `/v1/macro/series`, `/v1/macro/intraday/series`, and the options expiry, max-pain and OI distribution routes. A field that can be `null` is typed so in the schema; any other field is never `null`.
- **Units.** `*_pct` = percent (58.5 = 58.5 %), `*_ratio` = a dimensionless quotient (a share of a whole is a fraction, 0.585 = 58.5 %; `put_call_ratio` 1.2 = 1.2 puts per call), `*_bps` = basis points, `*_usd` = USD (every USD amount ends in `_usd`), `*_s` = seconds, `*_pp` = percentage points. Prices are in the quote currency (USDT for BTCUSDT). Volumes and quantities (`volume`, `buy_volume`, `sell_volume`, `net_volume`, `oi`...) are in BASE ASSET units (BTC for BTCUSDT), never dollars: a quantity without a unit suffix is in base asset units. A name without a market suffix covers EVERY market of the route: on a candle, `volume` is spot + perpetual futures, `volume_spot` and `volume_futures` one market each. Every response schema carries each field's unit in `x-unit`. Numbers are rounded to 12 significant digits.
- **Names.** One concept has one name on every route, in the snapshot, in the MCP and on the WebSocket: `buy_volume` / `sell_volume` / `net_volume`, `trade_count`, `sample_count`, booleans `is_*`, a qualitative reading `label`, instants `*_at`, durations `*_s`; the perpetual market is `futures` everywhere. A TRADE is one execution (`/v1/trades/spot`, `/v1/trades/futures`, WebSocket `trades.*`); the candles aggregated from trades are `trades_kline` (`/v1/trades-kline`). `data_type` is the route's own name (`/v1/trades/avg-size/history` -> `trades_avg_size_history`), and a snapshot field is named after the route that serves the same data (`liquidations_cumulative`, `trades_kline@1h`). Every retired name and its replacement is listed in `x-renamed` at the root of this contract.
- **Market in the path.** A route that serves several markets takes the market as a path suffix: no suffix = every market (spot + perpetual futures), `/spot`, `/futures` (`/v1/cvd`, `/v1/cvd/spot`, `/v1/cvd/futures`; the same for `/v1/buysell/ratio`, `/v1/trades/avg-size`, `/v1/orderbook`, `/v1/trades-kline`). The envelope repeats it in `market`.
- **Time.** Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds (`2026-09-28T14:00:00.000Z`). `time` is the canonical key: every timestamped object under `data` carries it. It follows ONE of two rules, and the description of `time` on each route says which. (1) A row of a BUCKETED series (candles, trade candles, CVD, order book per bucket, funding per 8-hour period, every `/history` read with `timeframe`) is dated at the START of its bucket. (2) A POINT-IN-TIME value is dated at the instant it refers to: the END of a rolling window (`/v1/buysell/ratio`, `/v1/liquidations/cumulative`, `/v1/oi/delta`), the instant of the computation (`/v1/basis`), the instant the SOURCE states (options, BTC, ETH, tokenomics; `/v1/global`, which may end in `.999`), the settlement a forecast is for (`/v1/funding/next`), the EVENT (trades, large trades, liquidations), and the most recent input of a composite (`/v1/macro/correlations`, `/momentum`, `/risk`, which also give `oldest_input_date` and a `time` per component). A daily value is dated at midnight UTC. The envelope's `server_time` is the time of the response. Time bounds (`since_ms`, `until_ms`) are epoch MILLISECONDS, inclusive.
- **Closed buckets.** Bucketed routes serve the last CLOSED bucket; `?live=1` adds the open one with `is_closed: false`. Every `/history` row carries `is_closed`.
- **Pagination.** A paged response carries `next`: the relative URL of the following page, ready to call (`/v1/klines?symbol=BTCUSDT&timeframe=1h&limit=100&before_ms=…`), or `null` once the range is read. Loop `while next: GET base + next`; it never repeats a row.
- **Freshness.** A response is never more than 1 second old (`Cache-Control: private, max-age=1`). `x-update-frequency-seconds` on each operation says how often the SOURCE changes — from 2 s (trades) to 5 min (daily macro, on-chain, ETF series): polling faster than that returns the same values.
- **Strict parameters.** An undeclared or repeated parameter is a 422 with a suggestion (`limt` -> did you mean `limit`?). `?fields=a,b.c` projects `data`.
- **Aggregation only.** No route discloses which venue a number came from, except the inter-venue spread, whose purpose is to compare venues.
- **Browsers and probes.** The REST API answers CORS (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, the `X-API-KEY` header allowed, preflight `OPTIONS` without a key) and `HEAD` on every `GET` route. A key used in a web page is readable by its visitors: use a dedicated key there.

## Errors

Every error has one shape:

```
{"status": "error", "server_time": "2026-09-30T14:07:27.808Z",
 "error": {"code": "invalid_symbol", "message": "Unknown symbol 'BTCUSD'. Accepted values: ...", "param": "symbol"}}
```

Branch on `error.code` (stable, listed in the `Error` schema), show `error.message` (English). Plan refusals also carry an `X-Deny-Reason` header (`key`, `family`, `websocket`, `rate`, `quota`, `depth`); 429 and 503 carry `Retry-After`.

## Limits

Each plan has a per-minute rate, a monthly quota and a history window per timeframe. Responses made with a metered key carry the IETF `RateLimit-Policy` and `RateLimit` headers. Going further back than your plan allows is a 403 `history_depth`, never a silently truncated answer. Details: https://bytnode.com/docs/rate-limits.

## Versioning

The URL prefix `/v1` is the API generation. `info.version` is the revision of THIS contract, in semantic versioning: a MINOR increment adds (a route, a field, a parameter, an accepted value), a MAJOR increment removes, renames or changes a meaning. Every response carries it in the `BytNode-Contract-Version` header, so a client detects a new contract without re-reading it. 2.0.0 (2026-10-12) covers the renamings published from 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-12 under 1.2.0: every retired name and its replacement is in `x-renamed`, the removal date of each route, parameter and snapshot field in `x-removed-on`, and a retired name answers with an error that names its replacement and the date. The guide: https://bytnode.com/docs/versioning. Adding routes, fields or parameters is not a breaking change. A breaking change is announced in the changelog (https://bytnode.com/docs/changelog) with notice by plan: Traders 30 days, Financial 60 days, Startup 90 days, Enterprise per contract.

## Links

Docs https://bytnode.com/docs · Pricing https://bytnode.com/pricing · Full reference for LLMs https://bytnode.com/llms-full.txt · WebSocket `wss://api.bytnode.com/ws` · MCP `https://api.bytnode.com/mcp` · Contact contact@bytnode.com

tags.name: System
tags.description: Health, per-feed freshness, the list of served symbols and what each symbol supports. `/v1/health` is the only route that needs no key.

tags.name: Snapshot
tags.description: One request, up to 48 fields for one symbol: the fastest way to fill a dashboard or give an AI agent full market context. Each field is `name=depth` (`funding_rate=1`, or `true` for depth 1); multi-timeframe fields are `name@tf=depth` (`klines@1h=24`, `cvd@1h=24`). Call it with only `symbol` to list the fields your plan includes.

tags.name: Market: prices & volumes
tags.description: OHLCV candles, individual trades, price change and the aggregated order book. OHLC comes from one reference spot market per symbol; a candle's `volume` covers spot and perpetual futures, `volume_spot` and `volume_futures` one market each.

tags.name: Order flow
tags.description: Who is buying and who is selling: trade candles (`trades-kline`: spot, futures, combined), CVD, buy/sell ratio, average trade size and inter-venue spread. Every bucketed series says whether the value is final (`is_closed`).

tags.name: Derivatives
tags.description: Perpetual futures positioning, aggregated across venues: funding (settled, estimated, cumulative), basis, open interest.

tags.name: Liquidations
tags.description: Forced liquidations across venues: individual events, cumulative long/short USD, big vs small liquidations, and the liquidation heatmap clusters the price is drawn to.

tags.name: Tokenomics & sentiment
tags.description: Supply, market cap and FDV derived from the live price; total crypto market cap and dominance; the Crypto Fear & Greed Index.

tags.name: Macro
tags.description: Daily FRED series (rates, inflation, liquidity, commodities, the VIX, US indices), intraday macro candles (ICE dollar index, EUR/USD, USD/JPY, gold, WTI oil), and derived crypto-macro signals: net liquidity, BTC correlations, macro momentum, risk-on/risk-off score.

tags.name: ETF
tags.description: Spot BTC and ETH ETF fundamentals per issuer, anchored on SEC EDGAR filings: shares, NAV, net assets and coins held.

tags.name: Options
tags.description: BTC and ETH options aggregated across venues: open interest and volume (calls/puts, USD), put/call ratio, ATM implied volatility, max pain, per-expiry and per-strike views, OI-weighted greeks.

tags.name: Bitcoin network
tags.description: Bitcoin chain state: recommended fees, mempool, mining pool concentration, difficulty and the next adjustment.

tags.name: Ethereum
tags.description: Ethereum fundamentals: gas, supply and burn, staking and yield, DeFi TVL, ETH/BTC ratio and derived signals (deflation, supply squeeze, gas momentum).

tags.name: On-chain Bitcoin
tags.description: Daily on-chain valuation and activity: MVRV, NVT, active addresses, miner stress.

tags.name: Technical indicators
tags.description: 19 technical indicators computed server-side on the same candles as `/v1/klines`, several per request (RSI, MACD, Bollinger, ATR, Ichimoku...).

code.description:
Stable machine-readable code. Branch on it, never on the message.

- `depth_too_large`: A snapshot field depth exceeds its documented maximum.
- `edge_rate_limited`: Too many simultaneous requests from this IP address (edge anti-flood).
- `history_depth`: The requested history goes further back than your plan allows.
- `insufficient_data`: Not enough history to compute the requested indicator.
- `internal_error`: Unexpected server error. A retry with backoff may succeed; if it persists, report it with the response's X-Request-Id header.
- `invalid_api_key`: The API key is missing, invalid or revoked.
- `invalid_asset`: The asset is not served by this family. The error lists the accepted values.
- `invalid_channel`: WebSocket: the channel name is malformed or unknown; the error lists the accepted forms.
- `invalid_depth`: A snapshot field depth is not a positive integer.
- `invalid_indicator`: The POST /v1/indicators body is invalid (id, type or parameters).
- `invalid_message`: WebSocket: the message is not a readable JSON object.
- `invalid_parameter`: A parameter has an invalid type or value.
- `invalid_series`: The macro series does not exist. See the family's /series catalogue.
- `invalid_symbol`: The symbol is not served. The error lists the accepted values (see /v1/symbols).
- `invalid_time_range`: since_ms / until_ms are not valid epoch milliseconds, or since_ms >= until_ms.
- `invalid_timeframe`: The timeframe is not accepted by this route.
- `method_not_allowed`: The route exists but not with this HTTP method.
- `missing_expiry`: The route needs an options expiry; the error lists the active ones.
- `missing_parameter`: A required parameter is missing.
- `not_applicable`: WebSocket: the channel has no meaning for this asset (a futures channel of a stablecoin). The REST API answers such a request with 200 and `unavailable: not_applicable`.
- `not_authenticated`: WebSocket: no key was presented at the handshake.
- `not_found`: Unknown route.
- `plan_family`: Your plan does not include this data family.
- `plan_websocket`: Your plan does not include the WebSocket stream.
- `quota_exceeded`: Your plan's monthly quota is exhausted.
- `rate_limited`: Your plan's per-minute rate is exceeded. Retry after Retry-After seconds.
- `repeated_parameter`: A parameter appears more than once.
- `service_unavailable`: Temporary unavailability. Retry after Retry-After seconds.
- `timeframe_not_served`: The series exists but does not serve this timeframe.
- `unknown_field`: A ?fields= or snapshot field name does not exist.
- `unknown_parameter`: The route does not declare this parameter.
- `upstream_timeout`: The request took too long. Reduce the window or depth, then retry.

ranges.description: One entry per price range around the mid price, from the tightest (±0.25 %) to the widest (±10 %). Each range is cumulative: ±1 % includes everything inside ±0.5 %.

time.description: The instant of the row — the ONE time key of every timestamped object, so a generic client needs one key. Two rules, and every route follows one of them. (1) A row of a BUCKETED series (candles, trade candles, CVD, order book per bucket, funding per 8-hour period, any `/history` with `timeframe`) is dated at the START of its bucket: a 1h bucket at 14:00 covers 14:00:00 to 14:59:59.999. (2) A POINT-IN-TIME value (a latest value, a rolling window, a forecast, a source snapshot) is dated at the instant it refers to: the end of a rolling window, the settlement a forecast is for, the instant stated by the source, the most recent input of a composite. The route's description of `time` says which. Always a date-time: a daily value is dated at midnight UTC (`2026-10-06T00:00:00.000Z`).

period_end.description: End of the period the row covers (exclusive): for funding, the instant of the settlement that pays the 8-hour period.

settled_at.description: Instant of the last settlement counted in the window: `period_end` for a complete settled window, earlier for the window in progress (`?live=1`).

rate_pct.description: Settled funding rate of the 8-hour period, in percent (0.01 = 0.01 % per 8 h), normalised to 8 h and open-interest weighted across venues.

is_closed.description: `true` = the bucket is final and will never change; `false` = provisional (only with `?live=1`).

post.description: POST a JSON body: `symbol`, `timeframe`, `limit` (values per indicator, 1 to 1000, default 1; `results` is accepted as a synonym) and `indicators`, a list of `{id, type, <parameters flat>}` — e.g. `{"id": "rsi_14", "type": "rsi", "period": 14}`. `id` is your own name for the result (1 to 64 characters among letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`), unique in the call: `data.indicators` is keyed by it, and a type may appear any number of times. A nested `"parameters": {...}` object is also accepted; an unknown body field is a 422 `unknown_parameter`. Computed on the same candles as `/v1/klines`; `limit + warm-up` is capped at 1000 candles. Each result gives `values` OLDEST FIRST (the order of a chart) with `times`, the candle of each value, and `time`, the candle of the last one. Errors on the indicators are 422 `invalid_indicator`. On a stablecoin: 200, `data: null`, `unavailable: "not_applicable"`.

parameters.name: limit

get.summary: Many fields for one symbol in one request
get.description: 48 fields for one symbol in a single call (40 plain, 8 multi-timeframe): prices, flow, derivatives, liquidations, macro, on-chain, options. Each query key is a field and its value a depth: `funding_rate=1` (or `=true`). Multi-timeframe fields take `@tf`: `klines@1h=24`, `cvd@1h=24`; `klines` also takes `1w`. Every field has the name and the response of its route: at depth 1, the object of a latest-value route (`basis`, `cvd@1h`, `orderbook@1m`…); above 1, the list of its `/history`; a field whose route serves only its latest value accepts depth 1 alone (422 `depth_too_large` beyond). A market field serves all markets (the route without `/spot` or `/futures`). Call it with only `symbol` to get `available_fields` (fields without a timeframe), `available_multi_tf_fields`, `timeframes`, `timeframes_by_field` and `max_depth`. An empty field carries `unavailable` (`not_applicable`, `no_api_key` or `no_data`) so 'no measure' is never mistaken for 'nothing happened'. Response: `symbol`, `data` (an object keyed by field name) and `partial` (true if a field failed).

get.description: Spot executions ("trades") across venues, one row per trade, most recent first — the same trades, with the same `id`, as the WebSocket channel `trades.spot`. Kept 72 hours; your plan sets how far back you can read. Without range parameters: the last `limit` trades. To read a time range, give `since_ms`, `until_ms` and/or `order` (`asc` or `desc`): a page holds at most `limit` trades and covers at most 15 minutes, and `next` is the URL of the following page — call it as is — or `null` once the range is read. Following `next` returns every trade of the range exactly once, in order. Each trade has a stable `id`, the same as on the WebSocket.
